## White text on an accent surface, and the limit of "the gate is green" (#1299)

**This section is below the manual marker deliberately.** It is the only record
of the pairs listed at the end of it, and everything *above* the marker is
replaced wholesale by `renderReport()` on the next
`A11Y_UPDATE_BASELINE=1 npx playwright test e2e/a11y-scan.spec.ts` — which is
the very command this file tells the next person to run. A note about
deliberately-deferred findings cannot live in the generated half.

#1299 named six pages and six selectors from the original #862 scan.
Re-measured on `main`: all six nodes were already fixed — `#mode-switch-label`
is `text-gray-600` (7.56:1), the portal's yellow hint is `text-yellow-800` on
`bg-yellow-50` (6.62:1), and the `text-gray-400` empty states are covered by
#2131's token raise (4.83:1 on white). So nothing came *out* of the baseline: it
was already `{}` on every key, and this report's counts are unchanged.

What the re-measurement did find is that the same *rule* had returned to the
same pages at new nodes, and that a green gate is not the same as a measured
one:

- `/portal` — the missing-documents CTA (`bg-amber-600`, 3.19:1) and the
  journey tracker's completed-stage check mark (`bg-green-500`, 2.28:1, a 1.4.11
  failure axe's *text* rule cannot see) are both behind fixtures the scan does
  not create.
- `/admin`, `/admin/candidates` — the admin nav's offer badge (`bg-amber-500`,
  **2.15:1**) and application badge (`bg-red-500`, 3.76:1) need a pending
  application or an outstanding offer to render; `LanguageBadge`'s unset variant
  needs a candidate, and failed in *both* themes (4.39:1 light, 3.04:1 dark).
- `/auth/signin`, `/rsvp/<token>`, `/messages` — the demo quick-login buttons,
  the RSVP accept button and the composer's send affordance are all reachable
  with no account, and all three carried the pair; none of them is in the
  sixteen pages the scan walks.

**The gate-skipping failure mode is the durable lesson.** The "Accessibility
regression gate" step in `e2e.yml` runs unconditionally, but it runs *after* the
smoke step — so on a job whose smoke step fails, the gate never runs at all and
the PR's red tick says nothing about accessibility. A failed step earlier in
that job silently disables this gate. That is why the cheap half of the rule was
moved out of Playwright entirely (see below).

Fifteen call sites of that one pair — solid `bg-<hue>-500`/`-600` under
`text-white` — were moved one shade down (red-600 4.83:1, amber-700 5.02:1,
green-700 5.02:1; the app's own `bg-blue-600` primary button is 5.17:1 and was
always fine, which is where the threshold comes from).

### What now guards it, and what each guard cannot see

| Guard | Covers | Blind to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm run check:contrast` (`scripts/check-contrast.mjs`, in `ci.yml`) | `text-white` over a solid `bg-*-N` in a className attribute or a class map, including a background in a ternary arm under an unconditional white label. No browser, no database, under a second — so no earlier failing step can skip it. | Translucent surfaces (`bg-red-500/40`), inherited and composited backgrounds, the dark remaps in `globals.css`, and any pair that is not white-on-accent. Also, by design, a white label that is itself conditional in one arm with the background in another — pairing those reports the ordinary toggle at a fictional 1.02:1, and a gate that cries wolf gets bypassed. |
| `e2e/contrast-1299.spec.ts` | The rendered result in both themes for the public RSVP buttons (green-700, red-600), the bell's unread badge (red-600) and `LanguageBadge`'s unset variant — the last of which is the one fix here that is *not* a white pair and so has no static cover at all. | Anything needing a fixture it does not build. |
| `scripts/test/contrast-guard.test.mjs` (`npm run test:unit`) | The guard's own two failure modes, pinned in both directions: too narrow (the split template-literal shape, which the first version missed on a site it had just fixed) and too broad (the toggle false positive). | — |

A per-file revert sweep over this change puts the static guard at 12 of the 13
touched files; the miss is `LanguageBadge`, which is a gray-on-gray pair the
guard does not model and the e2e spec asserts instead.

### Deliberately not fixed here — recorded so the next audit need not re-derive them

Both are a *different* pair on pages #1299 does not name, and folding them into
`check:contrast` would have it fail on code this change does not touch:

- **Mid-tone accent text on a light `bg-*-100` chip** — the icon containers on
  `/` and `/features`, 2.86-4.24:1. Above the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a
  glyph, below the 4.5:1 that 1.4.3 asks if one ever carries text.
- **`text-gray-500` on `bg-gray-100`** — 4.39:1, seven call sites across the
  projects, messages and todo surfaces.
- **`StatCard`'s value/label pairing** is a 1.4.11 item, not a text-contrast
  one, and is untouched.
- **Two white-on-accent glyphs survive on purpose**:
  `src/app/mentor/feedback/page.tsx` lines 93 and 104 put white icons on
  `bg-blue-500` (3.68:1) and `bg-purple-500` (3.96:1). Both are decorative
  glyphs, so 1.4.11's 3:1 is the applicable threshold and both clear it.


## Manual assistive-technology review — board and calendar (#2047)

An empty axe report is not an AA claim. Three WCAG categories are structurally
out of axe's reach — **4.1.3 Status Messages**, **1.4.10 Reflow** and anything
that depends on how a screen reader actually *behaves* — and this section is
where they are accounted for. `e2e/a11y-scan.spec.ts` regenerates everything
above this marker and carries this section over untouched.

### Status of this review — read this first

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Source-level accessibility review of the board and calendar** | Done — 2026-09-03 |
| **Reflow measurement at 320px and 400% zoom** | Done — automated, `e2e/mobile-layout-audit.spec.ts` |
| **Screen-reader session (NVDA or VoiceOver)** | **NOT PERFORMED** |

The screen-reader session has not happened. The work above was prepared in a
headless container with no audio, no screen reader and no desktop browser, so
nobody has yet *listened* to the board or the calendar. Everything in the
findings table below was derived by reading the components and their rendered
semantics, and each row says so. That is genuinely weaker evidence than a
recorded session: a source review predicts what an AT should encounter, it does
not observe what NVDA or VoiceOver does with it.

**If you are filling in a VPAT (#2037): this section supports 1.4.10 with test
evidence, and supports 4.1.3 with implementation plus an e2e assertion
(`e2e/live-region.spec.ts`). It does not yet support a "manual AT testing
performed" claim.** Say so rather than rounding up — a manual-testing row with
nothing behind it is the first thing an auditor pulls on.

### The session to run, verbatim

Run it, then replace the "NOT PERFORMED" row above with the versions and date,
and add what you found to the table. The point of writing the task list down is
that the next person repeats this run rather than inventing a different one, so
the results can be compared.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Screen reader + version | _(NVDA 20xx.x on Windows, or VoiceOver on macOS xx.x)_ |
| Browser + version | _(Firefox/Chrome for NVDA; Safari for VoiceOver)_ |
| Date | |
| Tester | |

**Board — `/admin/board` and `/mentor/board`, desktop width and 375px:**

1. Reach the board's first card using only the keyboard, and read out its
   mentee, its stage and its interaction count.
2. Move that card to another stage without a mouse (the per-card stage select is
   the drag-and-drop alternative) and say what, if anything, is announced.
3. Reach a stage column that is off-screen to the right — including an **empty**
   one, which holds nothing focusable.
4. Type in the board search and report whether the number of matches is spoken,
   how long after typing stops, and whether it repeats itself while you keep typing.
5. Collapse and expand a stage group; report whether its expanded state is spoken.

**Calendar — `/admin/calendar`, `/mentor/calendar`, `/portal/calendar`:**

6. Read the current month's grid: pick out today, a day with two events, and a
   day belonging to the previous month.
7. Open a day and read its events, then return to the grid.
8. Switch from month to week to agenda; report whether the arrow keys do
   anything, and whether the change of view is announced.
9. Step to the next and previous month; report whether the new month is announced.
10. Reload with a throttled connection and report what, if anything, is said
    while the calendar is loading and when it finishes.

### Findings

Severity is this project's own scale, not axe's. "Source review" in the last
column means the finding comes from reading the markup, not from a screen reader.

| # | Surface | Finding | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Board | The horizontally scrolling column strip (`HorizontalScrollArea`) could not take focus, so a keyboard-only user could not scroll a column into view whenever the strip held nothing focusable — an **empty** stage column is exactly that case (axe calls this `scrollable-region-focusable`; it never fired because the scan does not visit `/*/board`). | moderate | **Fixed** in #2047 — the scroller becomes a named, focusable `region` *only while it can actually scroll*, so a board whose columns already fit gains no dead tab stop. Source review. |
| 2 | Board (admin) | Typing in the board search re-filtered every column with no focus move and no announcement — the result count was a visual-only change (WCAG 4.1.3). | moderate | **Fixed** in #2047 — announced through the app-wide live region, debounced and de-duplicated (`useFilterAnnouncement`). Source review. |
| 3 | Account settings | The green/red save banner is mounted *together with* its text (`{msg && <div…>}`), and a live container that appears at the same instant as its content is not announced. Focus does not move on save either, so the outcome of every save was silent. | serious | **Fixed** in #2047 — `flash()` also announces. Source review. |
| 4 | Forms (`Textarea`) | The character counter changes colour at 80% and at the limit and said nothing. | minor | **Fixed** in #2047 — the two threshold crossings are announced (never per keystroke). Source review. |
| 5 | Calendar | The month grid's day cells are buttons named only by their day number plus whatever chips they contain: the 17th is announced as `"17"`, with no weekday, month or year, and outside-month days are indistinguishable. The cells are also toggles with no `aria-pressed`. | moderate | **Open** — filed as #2153. Source review. |
| 6 | Calendar | The view switcher is `role="tablist"` with `role="tab"` buttons, but there is no `tabpanel`, no `aria-controls` and no arrow-key navigation: it announces itself as a tab set that does not behave like one. | moderate | **Open** — filed as #2153. Source review. |
| 7 | Calendar | The view switcher answered its own overflow with `overflow-x-auto`, i.e. a sideways scroll inside a control that has no reason to need one — the four labels do not fit on one 320px line once translated (`Aylık/Haftalık/Günlük/Yaklaşan`, `Monat/Woche/Tag/Demnächst`). | minor (1.4.10) | **Fixed** in #2047 — the strip wraps instead; asserted at 320px in `e2e/mobile-layout-audit.spec.ts`. Measured. |

### What was verified as already correct

Recorded deliberately: these are the parts a re-audit should not re-litigate,
and breaking one is a regression.

- **Drag-and-drop has a real keyboard alternative.** Every board card carries a
  native `<select>` with an `aria-label` (`CardStageSelect`), which is also the
  touch path on a phone. Asserted end-to-end in `e2e/board-a11y.spec.ts`.
- **The board renders either the mobile list or the desktop columns, never
  both** (`useIsNarrow`). Nothing is duplicated in the accessibility tree — the
  usual `lg:hidden` trick would have every card announced twice.
- **The mobile board's stage picker carries its counts in the option text**
  (`BoardStageFilter`), so changing stage needs no announcement of its own: a
  native select speaks the option it lands on, count included.
- **The scroll fade affordances are `aria-hidden`** — they are gradients, not
  content, and they are not in the tab order.
- **The calendar's loading and error states already have live regions**: the
  loading overlay is `role="status"` with an `sr-only` label, the error branch is
  `role="alert"`, and `AsyncSection` follows the same split elsewhere.
- **The app has exactly one live region**, mounted empty for the lifetime of the
  page (`src/components/ui/LiveRegion.tsx`, provided in `src/app/providers.tsx`).
  Call sites announce through `useAnnounce()` instead of each inventing an
  `aria-live` container of their own — which is what makes announcements work at
  all, since a region that appears together with its text stays silent.

### How the automated half is covered

- **1.4.10 Reflow** — `e2e/mobile-layout-audit.spec.ts` measures `/admin/board`,
  `/admin/calendar`, `/mentor/board` and `/mentor/calendar` at **320×568** (the
  criterion's floor) and at **320×256** (400% zoom on a 1280×1024 desktop lays
  out in a quarter of each dimension), in **German and Turkish**, asserting the
  page never scrolls sideways. The rest of that file measures 360px and 768px
  with four stricter rules.
- **4.1.3 Status Messages** — `e2e/live-region.spec.ts` asserts the live region
  is in the DOM and **empty** on load, then receives the result count after a
  filter changes the page without moving focus.
- Neither spec is `@smoke`: they are regression nets, not critical paths, so
  they run in the scheduled full suite rather than on every push.
